evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/layout/admin.rs:15-20 (bad_request helper) returns StatusCode::UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY (422), and every admin handler funnels its DB failures through it: list_screens (:41,:45), get_config (:69,:74,:84,:88), put_draft (:118,:122), put_rails (:149,:153), list_manifests (:176,:180), put_manifest (:216,:220), publish (:247,:253,:271,:294), rollback (:319), kill (:356,:360), preview_resolve (:401,:407,:420), unkill (:449,:453). This maps infrastructure/connection failures (acquire_public() errors and sqlx query errors) to a client-side 4xx meaning 'your input is unprocessable'. Two concrete consequences: (1) a Postgres outage or pool exhaustion on any layout-admin endpoint surfaces as 422, which 5xx-based alerting/SLO monitors do not fire on -> DB outages are silently swallowed on this path; (2) API clients are told their well-formed request was rejected as invalid. Confirmed to be an oversight, not intent: the two SIBLING handler files in the same module handle identical DB errors correctly with StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR -- tenant.rs:28-35,:40-47,:51-58,:68-75,:206-213 and resolved.rs:35-40 (err500) at :70,:76,:80,:86,:95,:98,:103,:111. admin.rs reused its validation-error closure for infra errors too. Fix: give admin.rs a distinct err500 path (mirroring resolved.rs's err500 closure) for acquire_public()/repo DB errors, reserving bad_request (422) for the genuine parse/validation branches.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/layout/admin.rs:46,:123,:154,:181,:221,:296 and tenant.rs:214 -- successful responses are built with serde_json::to_value(row).unwrap_or_default(). On a serialization failure the .unwrap_or_default() yields serde_json::Value::Null, so the handler returns 200 OK with a body of literal null instead of a 500. A caller (ppt-web layout admin UI) that just performed a publish/rollback/put-draft/put-rails/put-manifest would receive a success status with no payload and no error signal, masking a genuine serialization bug as a successful empty write. Low severity because the row types reliably serialize today, but the pattern is a latent silent-failure across 7 write/read sites. Fix: map the serialization error to a 500 path rather than defaulting to Null (Json(serde_json::to_value(row).map_err(err500)?)).
